title: Onboarding Ignition Huddle - Copperline Logistics

Covered onboarding runbook, network/VPC requirements, data residency and retention, SSO and audit log needs, pilot success criteria, and next steps for a two-week pilot. Action items assigned for runbook updates, test dataset handoff, and a security docs review.

Pilot scope, success criteria, test dataset & benchmarks

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-09
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~44 minutes
Recording: available in CRM link

Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood CSM), Marina (Copperline Head of Integrations), Tom (VP Eng), Aisha (IT Security), Diego (SRE)

--- Summary (auto) ---
Jordan: quick kickoff, align on the two week pilot, scope, security items and network.

--- Topics ---
- Runbook and onboarding artifacts
- Private / VPC connectivity and firewall rules
- Data handling, KMS, retention, SOC 2 questions
- Pilot success metrics: latency, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy on routings

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey team, thanks for squeezing this in. I'm Jordan Cruz from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick intros?
[00:09] Marina: Marina Soto, I run integrations at Copperline. Nice to meet you all.
[00:12] Tom: Tom Becker, VP of Engineering. We're leading the pilot.
[00:15] Aisha: Aisha Rahman, IT Security. I'll be doing the security reviews.
[00:18] Priya: Priya Kapoor, Solutions engineer on the Red wood side — sorry Redwood — I'll be your primary SE for the pilot.
[00:24] Evan: Evan Lin, CSM, here to help with onboarding ops and runbook clarity.
[00:27] Diego: Diego Morales, SRE, I handle the networking side and infra.

[00:33] Jordan: Cool, objective for today is to align on the runbook, confirm what Copperline needs for network/VPC, what we need to hand off, and lock an initial pilot window. We'll also capture any blockers e.g. SOC2 or KMS things.

[01:05] Marina: Great, our timeline is fairly compressed. We want a working pilot in about two weeks, assuming no major security blockers. Main use case is automated document classification and routing for freight manifests.

[01:20] Tom: Right, and we need predictable latency under 350ms p95 for short requests, and cost guidance. We'll run this in our staging first.

[01:35] Priya: OK, that informs whether we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private. For your latency target and data residency, Private VPC deployment would be the conservative pick, but Dedicated in-hosted also possible. Quick question — do you have strict data residency or will staging in us-east be fine?
[01:53] Aisha: For staging we can use us-east. Production may need EU region later but that's future. Our main concern is encryption in transit and at rest, and audit logs for PII access.

[02:17] Jordan: Noted. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and have audit log hooks in the Console. We'll include sample config.

[02:29] Diego: On the networking side we'll need IP ranges and a peering plan. Do you do VPC peering or do you prefer private links?

[02:35] Priya: We support both patterns. VPC peering is simpler for many customers; we also provide a Private deployment package for VPC + NAT. We'll send a network checklist with the exact ports (gRPC/HTTPS) and IP ranges.

[02:50] Tom: Awesome. On auth — we use SSO via SAML for console access. Will that map to RBAC in Redwood?

[02:58] Jordan: Yes, we integrate SSO SAML/ OIDC and map to RBAC roles. We'll share the SSO setup doc.

[03:10] Aisha: For SOC2, are you able to share the current report or at least the SOC2 scope and what controls you have around encryption and access?

[03:21] Evan: We can share the SOC 2 summary and a security pack. We'll redact any customer specifics but it contains the controls, encryption, and data retention policies.

[03:31] Marina: Perfect — that helps. Also curious about tokenization or PII scrubbing. We may prefer to scrub PHI before it leaves our network. Is there a recommended approach?

[03:45] Priya: Many customers do client-side redaction or a local preprocess step in the SRE pipeline before sending to Redwood. We can also configure prefix-filtering and caching to minimize exposure. We'll add examples.

[04:05] Diego: About cert rotation and service accounts — we prefer short-lived certs. Are service creds rotated automatically?

[04:12] Jordan: For hosted keys we rotate, for Private deployments you manage the keys but we support easy rotation via KMS. We'll include a recommended rotation cadence.

[04:27] Marina: Ok. For pilot scope, we propose: 2 weeks, staging only, 100K tokens/day synthetic peak, run our document classifier. Success criteria: p95 latency < 350ms, classification F1 > baseline by 5%, and cost per 1k tokens below projected threshold. Thoughts?

[04:55] Priya: That's reasonable as a pilot. We'll prepare a benchmarking plan and runbook to measure latency and per-token cost. We'll also collect model selection suggestions — e.g., smaller quantized models vs larger ones depending on quality.

[05:12] Tom: We have an on-prem archive connected via VPN. If we need Private later, what's the path?
[05:19] Priya: We can do a gradual path: start hosted/dedicated in your region for staging, then once validated migrate to Private with VPC peering. We'll outline steps and estimated timeline.

[05:35] Aisha: Regarding logs retention — we need logs for 12 months for audit. Does Redwood retain request logs that long, and can we export them to our SIEM?

[05:46] Evan: Logs are retained per plan. For Private we can ship logs to customer-managed syslog or S3, and integrate with SIEM via an export. We'll document export hooks and retention config.

[06:04] Diego: Firewall rules — can you send exact egress IPs we need to allow?

[06:09] Priya: Yes, we'll include the IP blocks in the network checklist. For Dedicated sometimes IPs are stable per pool; for hosted they can be broader. We'll note the differences.

[06:27] Marina: Anything else on compliance? We might need a DPA and data flow diagram for legal. Can we get that?

[06:36] Jordan: Absolutely, legal pack and DPA template — we'll attach to the CRM and email.

[06:42] Tom: On instrumentation, we want per-route latency graphs in the Console and token-level cost breakdowns — do you expose that?

[06:51] Evan: Yes, Redwood Console gives per-route and per-model breakdowns, plus traces. We'll show you sample dashboards during the pilot demo.

[07:05] Marina: Great. Next — who will be the SRE contact for the initial work?

[07:09] Diego: That'll be me, Diego. I'll coordinate with Tom and Aisha.

[07:14] Jordan: Excellent. I'll summarize the runbook items: network checklist, SSO doc, KMS/rotation notes, log export, sample terraform, RBAC role examples, and benchmark plan. Priya will own the benchmark plan.

[07:29] Priya: For the benchmark plan, we need representative prompts, expected tokenization, and a few synthetic traffic patterns. Marina, can you share an anonymized sample?

[07:38] Marina: Yes, we'll scrub PII and send by Tuesday.

[07:42] Tom: On cost modelling — we need an estimate for the pilot and a projection for 10M tokens/month — can you provide simple calculators?

[07:50] Jordan: We'll include a cost worksheet. Note that batching and KV caching affects per-token cost; Priya can annotate the areas we can tune.

[08:02] Aisha: One security detail — we require that third-party processors support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. Does the Private option allow that?

[08:11] Priya: Yes, Private and Dedicated support customer KMS. For hosted, we provide managed keys but can discuss options. We'll include the specifics.

[08:24] Diego: Will you need any ports opened on our side other than standard HTTPS (443)?

[08:30] Priya: Typical is 443 for HTTPS endpoints. If using gRPC you may need specific ports; we'll call that out.

[08:40] Jordan: OK let's talk timeline: propose to start pilot week of 2027-03-21, two weeks. Security deep dive on 2027-03-11. Does that work?

[08:52] Aisha: 2027-03-11 works for our SecOps team.

[09:00] Marina: Week of 3/21 is feasible but will confirm on Monday once we have the runbook.

[09:07] Tom: On the pilot, who will own the test harness and metric collection?

[09:12] Priya: Redwood will provide a starter harness; Diego or your SRE will run it in your staging. We'll collect traces and logs back to the Console.

[09:24] Jordan: Quick note on models: we can suggest quantized smaller models that meet latency and reduce cost; we'll run quality probes. Priya will recommend which models to try first.

[09:36] Priya: Also we'll consider caching prefixes for repeated doc types to reduce token spend.

[09:45] Marina: Sounds good. Any blocker from legal?

[09:48] Jordan: We'll send the DPA and security pack; legal can review.

[09:54] Evan: I'll set up the CRM with next steps and attach artifacts: runbook, network checklist, SSO config, SOC2 summary, and the cost worksheet.

[10:03] Marina: Thanks. Quick question — does Redwood provide any training or onboarding sessions for our ops team?

[10:09] Evan: Yes, we offer a 60-90 min ops onboarding and a deeper technical workshop if needed. We'll propose dates.

[10:16] Tom: One more — do you support custom model rollouts and canarying? We may want to A/B different classifiers.

[10:24] Priya: Yes, the rollout tooling supports canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to another model variant. We'll include a short how-to doc.

[10:36] Marina: Ok that covers my main questions.

[10:40] Jordan: Great — recap of action items: Jordan to send runbook and terraform snippets; Priya to prepare benchmark plan; Aisha to kick off security details; Diego to provision VPC peering as per checklist; Marina to send anonymized dataset. We'll also schedule the security deep-dive for 2027-03-11 and tentative pilot start 2027-03-21.

[11:10] Tom: Thanks everyone. Any final Qs?
[11:14] Aisha: No, we'll review the pack and reach out if anything else.
[11:18] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up in CRM with the artifacts.

--- End transcript ---

References and shared artifacts:
- Runbook (to be attached): https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/copperline-onboard (placeholder)
- Security pack & SOC2 summary: attached to CRM
- Cost worksheet: will be shared via email

Meeting closed at ~16:14 UTC.
